title: while and do...while
learningObjectives: Explain while and do...while and choose an appropriate control-flow structure.

understand.concept: A while loop checks its condition before running the body, so it may run zero times. A do...while loop runs its body once before checking the condition, so it runs at least once.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the right loop depends on whether the body must run before the condition can be checked. Make sure the loop state changes so it can eventually stop.
understand.analogy: while checks the gate before entering; do...while enters once before checking the gate.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript control flow follows precise condition evaluation and iteration semantics.

explain.narrative: The while loop runs twice. The do...while loop runs once before its condition is checked.

examples.explanation: The while loop runs twice. The do...while loop runs once before its condition is checked.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the sequence or branch results described.

practise.guidedTask: Write one while loop that may run zero times and one do...while loop that must run at least once.
practise.independentTask: Write a small program that uses the control-flow structure to process learner or course data. Test normal, boundary, and empty cases.
hints: Use strict comparisons for exact values.
Choose for...of for iterable values and avoid confusing keys with values.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>while and do...while</title></head><body>
<script>let attempts=0;while(attempts<2){console.log('Attempt',attempts+1);attempts++;}let menuChoice=0;do{console.log('Show menu once');menuChoice++;}while(menuChoice<1);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which loop always executes its body at least once?
questions.explanation: do...while checks its condition after the first execution of the body.

questions.prompt: What should you verify when writing a loop?
options: That its condition and updates allow it to terminate as intended
questions.answer: That its condition and updates allow it to terminate as intended
questions.explanation: Correct termination and boundary handling prevent infinite loops and skipped work.
